title: Your Agreements Are a Database You Can't Query — Hiral Shah, Docusign & Sean Sodha, NVIDIA
talk_summary: Docusign and NVIDIA describe a pipeline that extracts structured data (especially complex tables) from millions of agreements using a small purpose-built 850-900M-parameter VLM extractor (Neotron Parse) instead of large general-purpose VLMs, then serves it via a proprietary data model and search. The main transferable lessons are about using small specialized models for narrow extraction tasks and pre-processing at ingest rather than at query time.

takeaways.technique: Small purpose-built extractor instead of a large general VLM
takeaways.what_they_do: They route a narrow, high-volume task (table/layout extraction) to a tiny ~850-900M-param single-shot VLM rather than a multi-billion-param general VLM, reserving big models for other work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when you think VLM you generally think a multi-billion parameter model... This is a very small tiny C radio VLM. It's about 850 900 million parameter model.
takeaways.numbers: ~850-900M params; claimed 20x faster table extraction vs other open-source models

takeaways.technique: Pre-process at ingest, not at query time
takeaways.what_they_do: They pay compute upfront to structure documents once so later queries are cheap and fast, explicitly trading high-throughput batch processing against low-latency interactive Q&A.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you are heavy on the compute at the upfront side with all the OCR so you don't have to worry about it later on

takeaways.technique: Layout/structure-preserving extraction over naive line-by-line reading
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue generic extraction fails on tables because it reads text line-by-line and loses structure; a layout-aware extractor preserves reading order and table structure.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they're reading text line by line which breaks a lot of that concept within the table

takeaways.technique: Benchmark on accuracy-vs-performance Pareto curve for the target task
takeaways.what_they_do: They evaluate candidate models on a task-specific benchmark (table extraction) and track both accuracy and throughput, not just raw quality.
takeaways.evidence_quote: both on the paro curve of accuracy versus performance, we're make sure that we're going to be releasing a world-class models

takeaways.technique: Quantization and multi-token generation for serving efficiency
takeaways.what_they_do: They plan FP8/NVFP4 quantization and multi-token generation to push the performance side of the Pareto curve after accuracy is established.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this model is currently on FP16 but there are paths towards going on to FP8 and VFP4
